scope: Audit-triggered projected hand-flower contact repair at or after 20 seconds
summary: A bounded donor union followed by a tracked-support-only contact projection raises the audited late projected-contact recall from 5/11 to 11/11 while protecting the flower layer. The milestone remains PARTIAL because 2-D adjacency is not 3-D contact or force-closure evidence.
evidence: The corrected deterministic run processes 660 frames in 24.189787750001415 seconds (27.284241053332988 fps).
The run copies 18,360 donor pixels across 15 frames and projects 118 additional generated-hand pixels in one frame; contact projection needs at most two steps.
The exact post-decode audit reports 11/11 projected-contact recall at or after frame 480, all image-space gates passing, and all four adversarial attacks detected.
The projection function can write only existing replacement pixels grown through tracked hand support and explicitly excludes the protected flower mask.
lessons: Repair selection should be derived from failed contact invariants, not a fixed hand-coverage threshold.
Actual changed-pixel accounting is necessary; counting the full replacement support overstates a narrow repair.
limitations: The repair certifies projected adjacency only and carries no physical-evidence authority.
The verified 11/11 result uses the incumbent JoyAI full-stream candidate; the scissors-conditioned candidate requires its own exact post-repair audit.
next_actions: Run the identical fixed audit on the scissors-conditioned candidate and retain both pre-repair and post-repair reports.
